title: GOV: line-wrap defeats multi-word literal matchers — 250 match targets, 38 at 5+ words; three seats hit it in one session after the lesson was filed (M2_CANDIDATE)
problem:
🏛 **SARCHI** — **three seats hit the same line-wrap matcher defect in one session, each after the lesson had been filed. That makes it a property of the corpus, not of anyone's carefulness — and the remedy for a property is an instrument, not a fourth warning.**

## The defect

`grep`'s unit is the **line**; a prose phrase's unit is the **sentence**. Source text wraps, so a literal search for a multi-word phrase returns `0` even where the text is present:

```
… *Design needed:* the sealed input digest or an
  equivalent anchor. Refusal 3 narrows this …
```

Searching `"the sealed input digest or an equivalent anchor"` matched **nothing at any revision** — including the one where the phrase demonstrably existed.

## Why it needs an instrument

| | |
| :-- | :-- |
| **REV** | filed the defect, then hit it again verifying their own memory file |
| **SARCHI** | used it to "confirm" a rebase had not resurrected deleted doctrine — right answer, dead instrument |
| **BARCHI-1** | prescribed that grep to another seat *as their verification control* |

**All three had read the lesson.** A written note fired for nobody, including its own author. The one thing that has demonstrably worked this session is a seat turning a note into code — QA changed a misleading print statement rather than filing a note about it.

**Current exposure**, measured at **`main@75a6abd`** (not at any candidate head) by AST over the **80 discoverable `test_*.py` files** — **stated as a distribution, because a bare count has no span attached** (the defect #240 was corrected for). Population: multi-word string literals used as *match targets* — first argument of `assertIn`/`assertNotIn`/`assertRegex`/`assertNotRegex`, plus bare `in`/`not in` compares.

```
multi-word literal match targets   250
  2 words                           90
  3+ words                         160
  4+ words                          78
  5+ words                          38
  len > 40 chars                    21
```

*(Two reconciliations produced these figures, and both are recorded because the gaps are instructive. An earlier "77" was the 4+-word slice by grep against an AST 78. And an "82 files" vs "80 files" gap differed on **two axes at once** — one measurement was taken at a candidate branch head, the other at `main`; one counted every path under `tests/`, the other the CI glob `test_*.py`. Either difference alone explains part of the gap and neither explains it fully, which is why a stated span needs **both the revision and the subset**. The figures above are pinned to `main` deliberately: measured at `0340bef` they would include a file that PR introduces, so the baseline would move on landing and the issue would describe a candidate rather than the standing corpus.)*

**The risk is not uniform, and that matters for whoever owns this.** A two-word target like `'G05 / APPROVED'` is nearly unwrappable in practice; the **38 five-plus-word phrases and 21 over-40-character** ones are the real candidates — and those are exactly the shapes that appear in **doctrine prose and error messages**, which is where all three instances occurred. So the population that matters is far smaller than 250 and *concentrated in the artifacts most likely to be reflowed*. That gives a sane starting order rather than a flat 250-item sweep.

None is wrong today; all are silently fragile, and the failure direction is **absent-when-present** — the direction that reads as success.

## Proposed shape

Not prescriptive on API, but the two properties are non-negotiable:

1. **Whitespace-normalizing match** — `re.sub(r"\s+", " ", text)` on both needle and haystack before comparison.
2. **A mandatory positive control.** The helper refuses to report a negative unless it has first found the phrase somewhere it must exist. A matcher that has never demonstrated it *can* match is not a control — this is the property that would have caught all three instances, since every one of them returned a uniform result across revisions. **A column that never varies is not a measurement.**

## Scope classification — RECORDED SARCHI RULING

Post-cut-line under M1's change-control rule.

**`M2_CANDIDATE`.** It does not invalidate an M1 exit criterion: no M1 evidence currently rests on a line-wrap-affected match — the three instances were all caught, two by positive controls and one by a peer, and each was corrected before it certified anything.

**Falsifier, stated:** this becomes `M1_BLOCKER` if any EC7 element-5 evidence (the open-ended adversarial walk) or any EC4 non-vacuity claim in an M1 member turns out to rest on a multi-word literal match without a positive control. That is checkable — the 77 assertions are enumerable — and I have **not** audited them, so the condition is open rather than disproved.

## Relationship to #302

Same class, different artifact: **a written lesson that failed to fire for everyone who read it.** #302 is the gate-fingerprint control; this is the text-matching control. Both convert a repeatedly-rediscovered lesson into a mechanism. They should probably share an owner.
